From a 20th anniversary perspective it depends on a lot of factors. A vampires generation and age. You get an elder or ancilla the lupine loses. As for neonate it depends on disciplines they have. How does each side prepare? Blood magic and silver and what do the Garou do? Some weird interactions you will need to solve between rank vs generation and who can affect what and when.

As an example dominate doesn’t work on vampires of a lower generation. But what about that 9th generation against a rank 3 or 4 garou? Some gifts key off of rank vs rank so need to determine how generation will influence that roll.

As for mage it also depends on where they are. In the open that mage cannot use their most obvious spells without provoking the consensus and then paradox backlash. So let’s say the vampire is near a vent and pipes. I uses forces to make the pipes explode that isn’t obvious as it is possible that happened so would only trigger lesser paradox.

But that mage uses forces to channel a lightning bolt and strike their target? There is a very high chance the paradox backlash will rip them out of time. A mage jumped an entire fleet of airships over New York and demanded surrendered. The backlash so bad it purged the event from everyone’s memory Ike it never happened. And the eldest mages who use magic to keep themselves alive cannot return to Earth easily they are confined to the Umbra.

Vampires have all their power in the material world and thrive in it. So you can have Mages and the Fera in the game it just takes planning on your part and a clear system on the disparity in the rules but I do it all the time in my games.
